_: A whole SCENE as ONE picture, where every other tool here draws a piece. The camp is drawn rather than carved out of a tileset — the user's call: 'build it not using the tile sets and just use art and then make objects clickable on it' — so what this file holds is the camp, and anything else a player LOOKS at rather than walks through.
_rules: (1) The COMPOSITION is load-bearing, because objects on it are CLICKED: say where each thing stands and keep the middle of the ground OPEN, or there is nowhere to put the character. (2) NO PEOPLE. The hero is drawn on top out of his own art, and a painted one is a second hero who never moves. (3) It is a BACKGROUND, so `no_background` is false and nothing may be a frame, a border or a UI panel. (4) Colours by exclusion as everywhere else, and the zone's own words: the camp is green meadow grass under near-black cliff rock.
_size: 688x384 is the 16:9 ceiling for `create_image_pro`, and at 2x it covers a 1376x768 stage. Bigger is not on offer.

camp.say: A small lived-in CAMP on a grassy shelf at the mouth of a cave, drawn as a game background seen from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE looking down and slightly forward. Across the TOP THIRD a sheer wall of near-black warm purple-brown cliff rock runs the full width, and a tall narrow SPLIT is torn open through the middle of it. OUT OF THAT SPLIT POURS WARM GOLD LIGHT: pale cream-gold at its core, deep amber further out, burnt orange where it washes the rock either side and spills down onto the grass in front of it, fading into the dark. It is the brightest thing in the picture. NOT violet, NOT purple, NOT blue, NOT cold. Set into the rock IMMEDIATELY either side of the split are FOUR sockets in TWO VERTICAL COLUMNS: two stacked one above the other tight against its LEFT edge, two stacked tight against its RIGHT edge, all four close to the light. NOT spread across the wall, NOT in a horizontal row. Each socket is a rough hollow CHISELLED out of the rock: an irregular angular recess with a jagged chipped rim, gripped by blackened iron claws bent over its edges that catch the gold light. They are empty and dark inside and no two are the same shape. NOT circles, NOT portholes, NOT round windows, NOT wheels, NOT identical. Below the cliff the ground is open short GREEN meadow grass, warm-lit where the gold reaches it. At the LEFT a heavy wooden work bench with tools and a vice on it. At the RIGHT a small ridge tent of weathered olive canvas with its flaps folded open, and beside it a tall wooden shelf stacked with jars and bundles. In the near FOREGROUND, low and slightly left of centre, a campfire of crossed charred logs burns bright orange in a ring of stones. THE MIDDLE OF THE GRASS IS OPEN AND EMPTY — nothing stands in the centre. NOT a village, NOT houses, NOT a castle, NOT masonry, NOT a road, NOT a person, NOT people, NOT a figure, NOT animals, NOT text, NOT a frame, NOT a border, NOT a user interface.

_seen: The FIRST round asked the split for violet and got it, and the user's answer was that the glow is the TITLE SCREEN's — measured off `shots/desktop-title.png`, that is pale cream-gold #fcde6f at the core, amber #f0a94b out from it and burnt orange #e08f37 where it washes the rock. The sockets came back as four evenly spread PORTHOLES; they are asked as two VERTICAL pairs tight to the split, chiselled and iron-clawed and no two alike, with `NOT portholes` in the exclusions. The hero reads right at x4 against a scene at x2 — x3 is small and x5 is big.
_limit: `create_image_pro` refuses a `description` over 2000 CHARACTERS, before billing. A scene's ask is long by nature — it places every object — so it runs close to that, and the cut always comes out of the exclusions rather than the composition.
